jobs.title: Integrations Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Merge is the leading provider of agentic tools and customer-facing integrations for frontier LLMs, Fortune 500 organizations, and B2B SaaS companies. Our platform offers three core products: Merge Unified, which enables businesses to add hundreds of integrations to their products with a single API, Merge Agent Handler, which empowers AI agents with secure access to thousands of third-party tools, and Merge Gateway, the control plane for running AI in production. Merge's enterprise-grade platform handles the entire integration lifecycle, from authentication and security to monitoring and maintenance. Thousands of companies trust Merge to accelerate product development, unblock sales, reduce customer churn, and save engineering resources—allowing them to focus on their core product.

*This role will be based in NYC five days a week. 

 

We are looking to grow our Integration Engineering team to help extend our reach across 7 categories in new and unprecedented ways!

 

This is a high visibility, high ownership role that plays a crucial part in Merge’s mission of powering integrations for all B2B companies. This role is perfect for someone who has a technical background and coding abilities, but also enjoys business-oriented problem solving at heart. We are looking for experienced engineers who are able to autonomously drive initiatives to improve the overall product experience. 

What you will do:

  • Own the technical strategy and execution lifecycle of integrations with our API providers - ideation, development, launch, and beyond

  • Work cross-functionally with partnerships, engineering, post-sales, and product to deliver enterprise-grade integrations & expand Merge's coverage across 7 categories

  • Internally advocate for Integration Engineering needs, and lead projects related to data quality and internal tooling

  • Help design the Integrations Engineering function at Merge - what it's responsible for, how it interfaces with other teams, and how it'll grow and develop over time

The ideal candidate will have

  • 1+ years in engineering roles, preferably with startup exposure

  • Strong technical understanding and problem solving, preferably in the form of a prior Computer Science background or other engineering orientation

  • Prior experience with APIs and integrations is a plus

  • Ability to manage responsibilities across different areas such as working cross functionally, debugging and building on APIs, or writing documentation

  • Bias to action & preference for being hands on -- Integrations Engineers work on powering mission-critical integrations for our customers, so we’re not afraid to jump in and become owners!

  • Strong communication skills, adept at interfacing with different audiences and communicating complex technical concepts

Compensation

  • The cash compensation range for this role is $115,000 - $145,000

  • Actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, and certifications. In addition to cash compensation, all full time employees receive an equity compensation package.

  • Lead a team of 5–8 engineers building new products from early traction toward product-market fit

  • Stay hands-on with technical decisions and architecture, especially in high-ambiguity or high-impact areas

  • Own the roadmap for your products, balancing fast experimentation with the reliability bar enterprise buyers expect

  • Partner directly with product, design, and GTM to turn customer signal into shipped product

  • Drive adoption of AI-enabled development and automation across the team

  • Build a high-performance culture centered on ownership, speed, and low-ego leadership

We're a high-growth Series B company selling into a fast-moving AI and developer ecosystem where the market changes weekly. Three product lines, three revenue models, and a GTM stack that has to keep up with all of them. RevOps here runs as an internal product team rather than a ticket queue. We build the infrastructure the revenue org depends on, and we own whether it works.

We're hiring a Senior Manager, GTM Systems to own that infrastructure end to end. You'll be the architect and the primary builder for Salesforce and everything wired into it: deal desk and CPQ, usage-based billing, partner reporting, and the agents we're putting on top of all of it. The work rarely arrives scoped. It usually starts as one sentence from a sales leader or the CFO about an outcome they need, and you come back with a plan, a timeline, and a system. If you want to design the machine rather than operate someone else's, this is the role.

What will you be doing?

  • Own the architecture of Merge's GTM systems (Salesforce object model, automation, permissions, data quality, sandbox and release governance) and be accountable for whether they're reliable, not just how they're configured.

  • Architect and ship net-new builds: CPQ and deal desk, quote-to-cash with Finance, and usage-based billing across product lines.

  • Build systems that hold. The measure is what keeps running when you're not touching it: automation with validation, monitoring, and test coverage in front of it, rather than workflows that need babysitting or re-fixing the same breakage every quarter.

  • Own change management end to end, not just the build. Project plans that work backwards from a go-live date, enablement for the teams who have to use the thing, legal and security intake, and a written record stakeholders can find without asking you.

  • Own the systems roadmap on a quarterly and annual horizon. Sit close enough to sales strategy and pipeline that when GTM direction moves, the systems implications are part of the decision rather than the cleanup.

  • Build with AI as the default method. Claude Code and agentic tooling to design, build, and audit systems; production agents that take real work off the GTM org's plate; and the judgment to know which problems are worth an agent and which aren't.

  • Own the GTM vendor stack: evaluation, procurement, implementation, and renewal negotiation.

  • Multiply the team. Documentation, permissioning, and tooling good enough that RevOps can triage and ship without you in the loop.

What experience is required?

  • 5-8+ years in RevOps, business systems, or GTM engineering, including 3+ owning a Salesforce instance as its architect rather than its admin.

  • You've run change management end to end on a system the revenue org depends on, whether that's the CRM, CPQ, billing, or the CS platform, including the migration, the enablement, and the cutover, without stopping the business while you did it.

  • Hands-on quote-to-cash: CPQ evaluation or implementation, approval and rate-table design, and a billing system wired to real usage data. Usage-based or hybrid pricing strongly preferred.

  • AI-native as a working method rather than a curiosity. You build and solution with Claude Code and agentic tooling daily, and you've shipped AI agents and automations that run in production with real users rather than demos.

  • Comfortable with AI-written code. You don't need to write Python or SQL from scratch, but you can read it, reason about what it's doing, direct an AI assistant toward the right approach, and verify the output is correct before it touches a live system. The correctness is yours either way.

  • A bias toward durable automation. You build things that hold under change, with validation, monitoring, and tests, rather than workflows that need you in the loop to keep working.

  • Project and stakeholder management as a real strength. You plan backwards from deadlines, write in the language of the person reading, and surface slipped timelines before anyone has to ask.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity as the default: you take a half-formed ask from an exec, return a scoped plan, and drive it without being managed through it.

Nice to have

  • B2B SaaS or developer tools, ideally multi-product with more than one pricing model.

  • Data warehouse, dbt, or BI experience; event-driven system design.

  • Clay, n8n, or hosted orchestration platforms for running agents and automations in production.

  • Vendor evaluation and procurement experience.

  • Marketplace or partner-sourced revenue (AWS, Tackle) and rev-share reporting.

  • The cash compensation range for this role is $170,000-190,000

  • Actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications. In addition to cash compensation, all employees receive an equity compensation package.

Technical Support Engineer at Merge
As a Technical Support Engineer, you will be responsible for providing high-quality support to our customers and prospects, including troubleshooting technical issues and assisting with integrating Merge into our customers' products. You’ll work closely with engineering and platform teams to debug issues, squash bugs, and prioritize customer requests. The ideal candidate will have a strong technical background with experience with APIs, excellent problem-solving, communication, and customer service skills. Your work as a Technical Support Engineer will be of high value and have a direct impact on the bottom line of Merge’s product offerings to our customers, with increased levels of internal and external visibility.

What you will do:

  • Provide top-tier support to customers via online chat, email, Slack/Teams and screen-share meetings.

  • Troubleshoot technical issues and drive creative solutions to customers in a timely manner.

  • Contribute to establishing and maintaining the integration of Merge into our customers’ product

  • Partner with Engineering, Product and Customer Success teams to resolve incidents and advocate for feature requests.

  • Create and maintain help center guides, runbooks, and internal notes to strengthen our knowledge base.

  • Help lay the foundation for a successful and rapidly growing support engineering team!

  • Take part in an overnight on-call rotation for critical incidents about once every six weeks.

The ideal candidate will have

  • 2+ years of experience in technical support, customer facing engineering, or solutions engineering roles.

  • Computer science background or other technical/quantitative orientation.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

  • Strong work ethic, a customer-first mindset, goal-oriented approach, and great attention to detail

  • Strong problem-solving skills; experience with scripting for debugging and one-off analyses is a plus.

  • Prior startup experience is a plus

 

Compensation

  • The cash compensation range for this role is $115,000 - $130,000

  • Actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, and certifications. In addition to cash compensation, all full time employees receive an equity compensation package.

Benefits:

  • Unlimited PTO + 10 company holidays

  • Quality health, vision, and dental insurance

  • 401K Plan

  • $200 one-time home office stipend

  • Free dinner when working past 7pm

  • Annual company offsites and quarterly team events. Past locations have included: Nashville, Sonoma, and the Hudson Valley

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Merge is the leading provider of agentic tools and customer-facing integrations for frontier LLMs, Fortune 500 organizations, and B2B SaaS companies. Thousands of companies trust Merge to accelerate product development, unblock sales, reduce customer churn, and save engineering resources—allowing them to focus on their core product.

Merge for Workforce gives companies control over how employees use AI. We need a Senior Product Manager who will treat this product like their own business: understand what a CIO will buy, build something employees will choose to use, and drive it from customer conversation to shipped product.

What will you be doing?

  • Own the direction of Merge for Workforce. Decide what to build, what to cut, and why.

  • Get close to buyers and employees. Learn what blocks a purchase and what would make the product indispensable.

  • Work in the details with engineering and design. Write clear specs, test the product, and push decisions through.

  • Join customer calls, study competitors, and keep the team moving as the market changes.

What you bring

  • You live in AI. You use the products, follow the people building them, and can name something you learned recently that changed your view.

  • You act without waiting. You see a gap, form a view, pull people together, and get something done.

  • You care about the work. You can point to something you pursued far beyond what was asked because you believed it needed to be better.

  • You have taste and technical depth. You can spot a weak experience, work through the tradeoffs with engineers, and make a clear call.

Compensation

  • Actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications. In addition to cash compensation, all employees receive an equity compensation package.
